commitResults.messageBody:
The starter project uses the Duke name and branding.

Rename the entry point and documentation to Groot, and replace the
banner to give the chatbot a consistent identity.

The chatbot only displays its banner and does not address the user.

Add a greeting, prompt, separators, and farewell to give each session a
clear beginning and end.

The chatbot exits immediately after greeting the user.

Read and echo commands until the user enters `bye` so a session can
support continuous interaction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add in-memory task storage and listing
commitResults.messageBody:
Echoed commands are not retained, so users cannot review earlier input.

Store task descriptions in memory and add the `list` command to display
them in insertion order.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to mark tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody:
Stored tasks do not record whether they have been completed.

Track completion state and add the `mark` command so users can update
and view a task status. Ignore generated Java build output as well.

Users can mark a task as done but cannot correct that status later.

Add the `unmark` command so a completed task can be returned to its
pending state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Encapsulate task state in Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Task descriptions and completion flags are stored in parallel arrays,
which can become inconsistent as task behavior grows.

Introduce a Task class that owns its description, completion state,
status updates, and display format. Store Task objects in one array.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add todo, deadline, and event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
All tasks share one generic representation, so dated tasks lose their
meaning and display details.

Add Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses and parse their respective
input formats. Record UI tests to verify polymorphic storage and status
updates.

Malformed commands can terminate the chatbot or corrupt task state.

Validate task details and task numbers, and report input problems
through a dedicated GrootException without ending the session. Add UI
coverage for invalid commands and confirm rejected input does not alter
stored tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task deletion with dynamic storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are stored in a fixed-size array, which complicates deletion and
capacity management.

Use an ArrayList to manage tasks. Add the `delete` command so users can
remove tasks by number, validate deletion input, and report the updated
task count.

Update the documentation and UI tests to cover task reindexing, retained
status, invalid input, and deletion from an empty list.

Command keywords are repeated as strings throughout parsing, which makes
the supported command set difficult to manage consistently.

Introduce CommandType to centralize keywords and argument rules.
Dispatch commands through the enum so invalid inputs remain distinct
from supported commands.

Extend UI tests with command boundary cases. Prevent invalid list or bye
arguments from changing or ending the session.

The README does not explain how AI tools contributed to the project.

Add an AI use section that records Codex's role in design,
implementation, testing, documentation, and Git maintenance. Clarify
that suggestions were reviewed and verified using Java 25 UI tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add file persistence for task list
commitResults.messageBody: Save task changes automatically and restore all task types and completion states at startup. Extend UI coverage with an isolated restart scenario to verify the saved data round trip.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden task persistence against data errors
commitResults.messageBody: Validate stored records, escape structural characters, and report read or write failures without stack traces. Save through atomic replacement and roll back in-memory mutations when persistence fails so disk and memory remain consistent.
Build and display the data path through java.nio.file.Path so separators remain platform dependent. Document and verify first-run behavior when both the data directory and task file are absent.

Validate deadline input as ISO yyyy-MM-dd, store it as LocalDate, and present dates in a readable English format. Preserve ISO dates through file storage and extend UI coverage for leap days, invalid dates, and restart loading.

Move command recognition, task construction, deadline validation, and task-index parsing into a dedicated Parser class. Keep Groot focused on application flow and task mutations while preserving every existing console response and persistence behavior.

Move collection ownership and task mutations behind a dedicated TaskList API. Give persistence an immutable snapshot and preserve explicit rollback operations so failed saves cannot leave the in-memory list inconsistent.

Group parsing, storage, exceptions, and task models by responsibility while retaining src/main/java as the source root. Update setup documentation and the AI-use declaration to reflect the new layout.
Point the application plugin at the packaged groot.Groot entry point so Gradle run starts this chatbot instead of the upstream template class.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for command recognition
commitResults.messageBody: Cover exact keywords, argument acceptance, argumentless commands, keyword boundaries, unknown input, and case sensitivity so parser command classification regressions are caught early.
Add whitespace and command-boundary cases for the highest-value CommandType logic. Document the approximately 50 percent high-value method target and require JUnit review after each code change.
Name the Shadow artifact groot.jar and explicitly set its packaged main class so it runs with java -jar. Document how to build, locate, and launch the artifact on supported platforms.

Document all public classes, constructors, methods, enum constants, exposed fields, and test methods while retaining the existing documentation for non-trivial storage helpers. Record the Javadoc assistance in the AI-use declaration.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align Java code with SE-EDU conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
Switch layout and collection naming do not fully match the project
coding standard, which makes the style inconsistent.

Indent switch cases, mark intentional fallthroughs, separate logical
blocks, use plural collection names, and adopt American spelling.

These changes improve consistency without changing runtime behavior.

Java changes need a consistent project-specific style reference that
agents can apply before handing work back.

Add a tracked skill based on the SE-EDU intermediate Java standard and
mandate it in the project agent instructions. Update the AI declaration
to record the assistance.

Commit preparation needs consistent message and branch conventions in
addition to the repository's authorization safeguards.

Add a tracked skill based on the SE-EDU Git guide and require agents to
apply it to future commit work. Preserve the rule that commits and
pushes require explicit user permission.

The coding standard branch contains the Java cleanup and the tracked
Java and Git agent skills.

Merge the branch without fast-forwarding so the standalone commits and
their branch boundary remain visible in the project history.
Keep project-specific agent skills available in the local workspace while excluding them from repository history. Remove their ignore exceptions and stop tracking the existing copies.

Users need a quick way to locate tasks without scanning the full list. Add case-insensitive description matching through the find command while preserving task order and list state. Cover parsing, matching, invalid input, and UI output with JUnit and console tests.
Integrate case-insensitive task-description search together with its parser, JUnit, console UI, and user documentation coverage.

Cover searches that have no matching task description.

Use an explicit void-compatible lambda for the missing-keyword
assertion.
